components.useFor: A headline or body sentence is long and a simpler single-unit entrance would feel flat.

components.name: Story Dip
components.description: Timestamped story lines, "Leo's film was one render away.", drift across the frame.
components.useFor: A short anecdote in three beats, such as setup, a snag and the fix, each with its own timestamp.

components.name: Stretch In
components.description: Letters fly in from off-canvas and smear horizontally on the way — a vertex-lag deformation, not a scale.
components.useFor: A heavy display word needs a fast, physical entrance where the letterforms visibly deform — bars stretch long while stems keep their exact width.

components.name: Strikethrough Replace
components.description: Draws a strike line across old text then reveals new text in its place.
components.useFor: Showing a problem being replaced by a solution — the strike says you are crossing this out on purpose

components.name: Stripe Mask
components.description: Slanted stripes mask a two-sentence bold headline into view.
components.useFor: A bold two-sentence statement that should be revealed through slanted stripes.

components.name: Stripe Type
components.description: A word cut into horizontal bands, as in the IBM logo, slides together from alternating sides and locks, then can pass on through.
components.useFor: A bold word needs a graphic, engineered entrance on a flat field, such as a product name or a section title.

components.name: Strobe Words
components.description: Big words strobe in at a set rhythm over a dark horizon glow, ending on the logo.
components.useFor: A fast opener that cuts through a list of verbs, such as Plan, Write, Render, Ship.

components.name: Tagline Justify
components.description: A tagline sets itself into a justified column with an italic gradient word.
components.useFor: A closing tagline that should lock up as a tidy poster block with a logo beneath it.

components.name: Tategaki Turn
components.description: Vertical Japanese-style text turns upright into a horizontal line, 'Read it both ways.'.
components.useFor: A tagline that plays on reading direction, with vertical Japanese-style columns turning to a line.

components.name: They Are You
components.description: Three "You ..." lines in orange and white describe the viewer on a purple ground.
components.useFor: An audience-recognition beat that describes the viewer in the third person, then turns it on them.

components.name: Three Steps
components.description: Three large gradient numerals light along a connecting line: Install, Compose, Render.
components.useFor: A how-it-works beat that explains the product in three steps, such as install, compose, render.

components.name: Tittle Drop
components.description: Dots of the i and j drop in last onto 'Ship it in minutes.' on a light ground.
components.useFor: A hero line for a launch video where a small, witty typographic detail makes the headline memorable.

components.name: Tldr on Top
components.description: A TL;DR summary sits on top of a long body paragraph that fades off.
components.useFor: A story beat that admits the full explanation is long and gives the short version first.

components.name: Top-Down Letters
components.description: Letters descend from above in a pronounced staircase, one symbol at a time, with zero blur.
components.useFor: A single uppercase word or short acronym should enter with structural weight — each letter landing like a stamp.

components.name: Torn Edge
components.description: A torn paper sheet rips away to reveal a bold headline printed on the gradient stage.
components.useFor: A reveal that rips a paper sheet away to show a bold headline underneath.

components.name: Tracking In
components.description: Letter-spacing collapses and blur clears with a springy motion.
components.useFor: A title word or brand name should feel like it is focusing into place — tracking collapse is the right metaphor for clarity, precision, or sharpness.

components.name: Turnabout
components.description: "The video works for you." with the last word turned to an orange accent.
components.useFor: A positioning beat that flips the framing, such as from effort for the tool to effort from the tool.

components.name: Two Hit
components.description: A two-hit headline, "Streaming now.", in white then blue, right-aligned on black.
components.useFor: A two-beat teaser where a first line is replaced by a second, like a premiere card.

components.name: Type Fossil
components.description: A readable word carries layers of fine contours, revises itself, then compresses into a clean typographic imprint.
components.useFor: A creative process should move from earlier wording to a finished idea.

components.name: Type Repeater
components.description: An After Effects style repeater on a word, where copies unfold into a tunnel, a spiral or a fan behind it, breathe, then fold back into the word.
components.useFor: One word should hit hard for a beat, with repetition giving it depth and energy around a still, readable center.

components.name: Type Wall
components.description: Rows of one word fill the frame, run in alternating directions at different speeds in heavy, narrow and outline faces, with an accent band through the middle.
components.useFor: A loud full-screen beat for one word, such as a section title, a manifesto word or a transition card.

components.name: Typed Split Wipe
components.description: A centered cursorless type build holds, then exits through opposing fixed-layout glyph wipes that leave the anchor visible longest.
components.useFor: A product or feature introduction should type itself cleanly before breaking into controlled directional fragments.

components.name: Typewriter
components.description: Character-by-character text reveal with a deterministic blinking cursor.
components.useFor: Simulating a command being typed into a terminal or input — pairs with `terminal-simulator`.

components.name: Typo Fix
components.description: A misspelled word is caught and corrected in place inside a short line.
components.useFor: A quick-edit demo showing how easy a copy fix is.

components.name: Uncomment Line
components.description: Three lines are uncommented one by one in code style: 'Fork the scenes. Change anything. Own the cut.'.
components.useFor: A developer-product beat where three promises should read like code being switched on.

components.name: Unmask Line
components.description: A monospace line is unmasked letter by letter, 'Out of stealth.', the last word in green.
components.useFor: A tech or developer-tool announcement where a monospace line is unmasked letter by letter.

components.name: Value Swap
components.description: Swaps a value in place with a vertical slide — the old value exits up as the new one enters from below while an invisible sizer keeps the width stable.
components.useFor: A value changes at a specific story beat — before/after price, status promotion, a hex/token flip.

components.name: Verbed
components.description: A dictionary entry for "remocn" with senses, inflections and an example sentence.
components.useFor: A brand-voice beat where the product name has become a verb among users.

components.name: Wake Wipe
components.description: A wake-like wipe reveals 'Ship the launch video today.' with a gradient accent word.
components.useFor: A three-line pitch where each line is wiped away by a trailing wake and the last carries an accent word.

components.name: Walkout Name
components.description: A fighter-style name stack, 'The Launch Kid', with a light slash, record and a serif nickname.
components.useFor: A launch-day intro beat that announces a founder or product by name with a nickname and a headline stat.

components.name: Waveform Title
components.description: A headline rises over an aurora waveform line that settles into an underline beneath it.
components.useFor: A product beat about voice, audio or captions where a waveform line sits under the title.

components.name: We Call It
components.description: Short lines build to "We call it a" and then a big orange "video registry.".
components.useFor: A category-naming beat where several loose descriptions resolve into one name.

components.name: Week Shipped
components.description: A week-recap line, "Sunday, we rested.", in heavy type on orange.
components.useFor: A weekly changelog video that recaps what shipped each day.

components.name: Weight Wave
components.description: A wave of font weight travels across a line of text and settles on a highlighted word.
components.useFor: A tagline about motion or flexibility where the type itself should feel alive.

components.name: What Sticks
components.description: A column of claims dims one by one until "You own every file." is highlighted.
components.useFor: A message-discipline beat that shows only one claim survives the viewer's memory.

components.name: Which Means
components.description: A feature tag, "Live preview", leads into a "which means" explanation in teal and white.
components.useFor: A feature beat that turns one capability into a chain of benefits.

components.name: Whole Page
components.description: A manifesto of six serif belief paragraphs fills a navy page in columns.
components.useFor: A mission or values beat for a long-form brand film.

components.name: Width Lock
components.description: A condensed line stays width-locked while a word swaps, 'Ship the launch video by tonight.'.
components.useFor: A claim with one slot that cycles through deliverables, such as trailer, captions, launch video.

components.name: Word Acts
components.description: Short acts of one word each, with changing styles, end on a gradient word.
components.useFor: A feature-list beat where each word demonstrates itself, such as stretching, splitting, heavy or fast.

components.name: Word Gap Media
components.description: A video tile slots into the gap between "Launch all" and "of this".
components.useFor: A beat where media tiles slot into a gap inside a sentence, such as showing the screens behind the claim.

components.name: Word Insert
components.description: A sentence edits itself, opening a gap and inserting a new word with a gradient.
components.useFor: A tagline that grows from a plain noun into a full promise.

components.name: Word Ladder
components.description: A word changes a letter or two per rung, climbing a ladder to the last word.
components.useFor: A transformation beat such as idea to ship in a few steps.

components.name: Word Pullback
components.description: The camera pulls back from a big word to reveal "The cinematic toolkit for every launch".
components.useFor: An opener that starts on one huge word and pulls the camera back to reveal the full sentence.

components.name: Word Push
components.description: A phrase builds from its first word centered: each next word drives in from the right and pushes the line left, easing into the new center.
components.useFor: A single tagline or closing phrase should build word by word with physical, push-driven motion instead of plain fades.

components.name: Word Stack
components.description: Caps words stack in a tight poster, the last one swapped for a serif gradient italic.
components.useFor: A manifesto or tagline beat of five to seven short words that builds one word at a time into a poster.

components.name: Word Stream
components.description: Voiceover-paced phrases that build word by word — the next word looms as a blurred ghost before it resolves, then the phrase cuts away.
components.useFor: An intro or narration follows a voiceover and each phrase should build word by word at speaking pace.

components.name: Wrapped Squash
components.description: Each caps line squashes to fill its own coloured block, stacking into a poster.
components.useFor: A recap beat of two or three short caps lines, such as a year-in-review or shipped-this-quarter summary.

components.name: Yes Run
components.description: "Free?" is answered by a black "Yes." tag on bright orange.
components.useFor: An objections-handling beat that says yes to a run of product questions.

components.name: Your Name Here
components.description: "A launch film for {yourProduct}." with a swap-one-prop caption on a red card.
components.useFor: A template-style beat that tells the viewer to drop in their own product name.

components.name: Zoom Words
components.description: A close-up word reveal: huge words fade into a long line while the camera rides the write head, the line streaming off-frame as the shot eases into focus.
components.useFor: An intro should open uncomfortably close: huge words appearing one by one while the camera tracks the growing line off-frame.

components.name: UI AI Prompt Flow
components.description: An AI prompt composition: a prompt types into the field, the Generate button runs hover → press → loading, a skeleton shimmer reveals, then crossfades into the generated answer, and a ready toast slides in. A pure orchestrator — the shimmer is owned by the skeleton-block motion atom; every other channel comes from a composed primitive's hook.
components.useFor: Demoing an AI product's whole prompt-to-answer experience in one self-contained scene

components.name: UI Chat Flow
components.description: A messaging composition: an outgoing message types into the composer, the send button presses, and the bubble rises in; the other side shows a typing indicator that swaps into the reply, and reactions pop in. A pure orchestrator — every channel comes from a composed primitive's hook (Input, MessageBubble, TypingIndicator).
components.useFor: A scene needs a messaging conversation that carries your own brand tokens instead of a real platform's chrome.

components.name: UI Checkout Flow
components.description: A cursor-driven checkout card: the card and its fields blur-in, then the pointer flips a billing-cycle toggle, types a card number, ticks the terms checkbox, and presses Pay through to success, ending in a toast. A pure orchestrator — every channel comes from a composed primitive's transition hook.
components.useFor: Demoing a SaaS payment or upgrade UX end-to-end with cursor navigation and toast confirmation.

components.name: UI iMessage Chat Flow
components.description: An iMessage-styled messaging composition: gray incoming and blue outgoing bubbles with tails, an in-thread typing bubble with dots, a Delivered label, and tapback-style reaction badges. The composer types the outgoing message before sending. Chrome icons come from lucide-react; self-contained otherwise, composing the caret and typing-indicator primitives.
components.useFor: The scene must read as iMessage — gray incoming and blue outgoing tailed bubbles with tapback badges at the outer top corner.

components.name: UI Onboarding Stepper Flow
components.description: A multi-step onboarding composition: a horizontal stepper advances through panels of input, radio, and switch fields, finishing on a Finish button that runs to success. Panel crossfade derives linearly from the stepper's exposed position channel; every other channel comes from a composed primitive's hook.
components.useFor: Demoing a multi-step onboarding experience — account setup, plan choice, preferences — in one scene

components.name: UI Settings Toggle Flow
components.description: A two-column settings card: the card and its controls blur-in, then the cursor flips a switch, opens a select, drags a labeled slider, and clicks Save, ending in a saved toast. A pure orchestrator — every channel comes from a composed primitive's transition hook.
components.useFor: Showing a complete settings interaction walkthrough for a product demo — zero assembly required.

components.name: UI Signup Flow
components.description: A signup card composition: a real shadcn-style card (header, labeled Full Name / Email / Password / Confirm fields, primary + Google-outline buttons, sign-in footer) whose cursor fills each field top-to-bottom, then clicks Create account (hover → press → loading → success) as a success toast slides in. A pure orchestrator — every channel comes from a composed primitive's transition hook.
components.useFor: Showing a full onboarding or signup flow in a product launch or demo video.

components.name: UI Telegram Chat Flow
components.description: A Telegram-styled messaging composition: tailed bubbles (white incoming, blue outgoing) with in-bubble timestamps and delivery checks, a header that flips to 'typing…' while the other side replies, reaction chips, and a Telegram composer that types the outgoing message before sending. Self-contained — it owns its timeline and only composes the caret primitive.
components.useFor: The scene must read as Telegram — blue tailed bubbles, in-bubble timestamps, and double-check delivery marks.

components.name: UI Accordion
components.description: A disclosure whose opened/closed state is a pure function of the timeline; the panel reveal, chevron, and background are keyframed presets.
components.useFor: Showing a collapsible FAQ or settings section expanding on a timeline cue.

components.name: UI Alert Dialog
components.description: A modal alert dialog whose opened/closed state is a pure function of the timeline; the backdrop dim and popup zoom are keyframed presets. Self-contained — pair it with the Button as a trigger (see the example).
components.useFor: Showing a destructive confirmation dialog (delete, reset, revoke) in a product demo.

components.name: UI Blur In
components.description: A wrapper that reveals a single child with blur + opacity + a directional offset; a pure state atom, theme-independent — its context is a motion config (blur/distance/axis), not a theme.
components.useFor: Revealing an arbitrary JSX subtree (card, image, composed scene) with a premium blur entrance.

components.name: UI Button
components.description: A button whose idle/hover/press/loading/success state is a pure function of the timeline; the loading state composes the Spinner motion atom.
components.useFor: Showing the full interactive lifecycle of a CTA — hover → press → loading → success — on the timeline.

components.name: UI Caret
components.description: A blinking text caret — a controlled vertical bar, or a pure motion atom that blinks deterministically from useCurrentFrame.
components.useFor: Placing a blinking insertion cursor beside a text node or at the end of a typed string.

components.name: UI Checkbox
components.description: A checkbox whose checked/unchecked state is a pure function of the timeline; the box fill, border, and checkmark draw are keyframed presets.
components.useFor: Showing a task being checked off in a to-do or onboarding list.

components.name: UI Combobox
components.description: A combobox whose opened/closed state is a pure function of the timeline; the panel fade/scale/lift are keyframed presets like select. The trigger reuses the Input presets (typed query + caret reveal via an injected inputStyle), the list is filtered by a pure case-insensitive substring on the visible query prefix, and rows reuse the SelectItem row.
components.useFor: Showing a searchable/filterable dropdown with a typed query narrowing the list on the timeline.

components.name: UI Command Menu
components.description: A ⌘K command palette whose opened/closed state is a pure function of the timeline; the panel zoom + backdrop dim are dialog-like keyframed presets. The search row reveals the typed query, the list is filtered by a pure case-insensitive substring on the visible query prefix, and rows reuse the CommandMenuItem row.
components.useFor: Demoing a ⌘K palette opening with a typed query filtering icon-labeled commands.

components.name: UI Context Menu
components.description: A right-click context menu whose opened/closed state is a pure function of the timeline; the panel scales from its top-left corner (the click point) with a fade + lift. No trigger — the caller positions it. Rows reuse the DropdownMenuItem row; items are plain string labels.
components.useFor: Showing a right-click menu appearing at a cursor position over content in a product demo.

components.name: UI Cursor
components.description: An animated cursor that moves between waypoints, clicks (ripple), and drags. The Cursor renderer is a pure function of a numeric CursorStyle channel; useCursorPath reads the frame and eases the path, ripple, and press phases.
components.useFor: Guiding the viewer's attention through a UI by animating a pointer between elements.

components.name: UI Dialog
components.description: A modal dialog whose opened/closed state is a pure function of the timeline; the backdrop dim and popup zoom are keyframed presets, with a close button and a primary action. Self-contained — pair it with the Button as a trigger (see the example).
components.useFor: Showing a non-destructive modal (edit form, settings, profile update) opening and closing on the timeline.

components.name: UI Drawer
components.description: A bottom panel whose opened/closed state is a pure function of the timeline; the backdrop dim and bottom-edge slide-up are keyframed presets, with a drag handle and a primary action. Self-contained — pair it with the Button as a trigger (see the example).
components.useFor: Showing a mobile-style bottom sheet sliding up from the edge of the frame.

components.name: UI Dropdown Menu
components.description: A dropdown menu whose opened/closed state is a pure function of the timeline; the trigger reuses the Button primitive and the reveal panel composes DropdownMenuItem rows. The panel fade, scale, lift, and chevron are keyframed presets.
components.useFor: Showing a button that opens an action list — the classic "Options" or account menu pattern.

components.name: UI Field
components.description: A static layout family for composing labeled form controls, modeled on shadcn's Field: FieldGroup ▸ Field ▸ FieldLabel / FieldControl / FieldDescription. Reads no frame and holds no state — colors come from the resolved theme. FieldControl is a relative fixed-height slot for the absolute remocn-ui controls (Input, Button).
components.useFor: Laying out labeled form controls — label, animated control, description hint — with consistent spacing

components.name: UI Input
components.description: A text input whose idle/hover/active/typing/invalid state is a pure function of the timeline; the focus ring, border, caret, and value reveal are keyframed presets.
components.useFor: Showing a text field being focused, typed into, or validated at a specific frame.

components.name: UI Message Bubble
components.description: A chat message bubble whose hidden/visible state is a pure function of the timeline. The renderer is a pure function of a MessageBubbleStyle (opacity, translateY, scale); useMessageBubbleTransition eases the rise-in enter. The incoming/outgoing variant resolves bubble color and alignment from the theme, and an optional reaction badge pops in on its own channel.
components.useFor: You are hand-timing a single message landing on a beat you control, driving `style` from `useMessageBubbleTransition`.

components.name: UI Popover
components.description: A popover/hover-card whose opened/closed state is a pure function of the timeline. The Popover renderer is a pure function of a PopoverStyle (opacity, scale, translate); usePopoverTransition eases both the open and the close. The static `side` prop sets the enter translate axis; renders title + description and/or arbitrary children in a popover card.
components.useFor: Showing a hover-card with richer content (title + description) than a single-line tooltip label allows.

components.name: UI Progress
components.description: A progress bar whose fill is a pure function of a numeric value channel (value-channel deviation). The Progress renderer takes a clamped 0–100 value; useProgressTransition reads the frame and eases the fill between value steps. Muted track + primary indicator, optional floored percentage label.
components.useFor: Showing a loading, upload, or completion bar animating to a target value.

components.name: UI Radio
components.description: A radio whose checked/unchecked state is a pure function of the timeline; the ring border and inner dot pop are keyframed presets.
components.useFor: Demonstrating a single-choice selection moment in a form walkthrough.

components.name: UI Resizable
components.description: Two panels split by a draggable handle, where the split ratio is a numeric channel plus a handle idle/hover/press channel (dual-channel value-channel deviation). The Resizable renderer is pure (clamped 0–1 ratio, handle scale, grab-ring opacity); useResizableTransition reads the frame and eases both channels — ratio as a numeric lerp, the handle visual from its state presets. Horizontal and vertical splits; 1px divider + centered grip pill with a derived grab ring.
components.useFor: Demonstrating a code/preview split pane layout with its ratio animating across frames.

components.name: UI Select
components.description: A select whose opened/closed state is a pure function of the timeline; the trigger reuses the Button primitive and the reveal panel composes SelectItem rows. The panel fade, scale, lift, and chevron are keyframed presets.
components.useFor: Demonstrating a dropdown menu opening and an option being highlighted or selected on the timeline.

components.name: UI Select Menu
components.description: A vertical option list where exactly one row is highlighted; the highlight bar and left accent slide smoothly between rows. Fully controlled via selectedIndex/state or useSelectMenuTransition.
components.useFor: A vertical single-choice menu where one option is highlighted and the highlight should glide smoothly between options as the selection changes.

components.name: UI Sheet
components.description: A side panel whose opened/closed state is a pure function of the timeline; the backdrop dim and right-edge slide-in are keyframed presets, with a close button and a primary action. Self-contained — pair it with the Button as a trigger (see the example).
components.useFor: Showing a slide-in edit panel or settings drawer with backdrop dim in a product demo.

components.name: UI Skeleton
components.description: A skeleton→content crossfade whose loading/loaded state is a pure function of the timeline. The Skeleton renderer is pure (reads no frame); only the composed SkeletonBlock shimmer reads it. SkeletonStyle opacities sum to 1 so the box never dims; real children sit in normal flow and the placeholder (a lines/card layout or a custom node) is an absolute overlay.
components.useFor: Showing a loading state resolving to real content — the skeleton fades out as real UI fades in.

components.name: UI Skeleton Block
components.description: A shimmer placeholder block — a motion atom (spinner pattern). A directional highlight gradient sweeps across deterministically from useCurrentFrame() and loops seamlessly. Configurable width/height/radius/speed and base/highlight colors.
components.useFor: Building a custom skeleton layout by composing individual shimmer rectangles at precise dimensions

components.name: UI Slider
components.description: A slider whose fill is a numeric value channel plus a thumb idle/hover/press channel (dual-channel value-channel deviation). The Slider renderer is pure (clamped 0–100 value, thumb scale, grab-ring opacity); useSliderTransition reads the frame and eases both channels — value as a numeric lerp, the thumb visual from its state presets. Muted track + primary range + bordered thumb with a derived grab ring.
components.useFor: Demonstrating a range control being dragged to a target value with hover/press thumb states.

components.name: UI Spinner
components.description: A deterministic spinning arc that loops on the Remotion frame — a pure motion atom with no state.
components.useFor: Showing a loading indicator inside a button after a click (hover → press → loading state).

components.name: UI Stepper
components.description: A horizontal onboarding stepper whose progress is a pure function of a continuous step index (value-channel deviation). Every circle (fill, number, stroke-dash check) and connector (primary fill fraction) derives purely from the float position; useStepperTransition reads the frame and eases position between step indices.
components.useFor: Showing a multi-step onboarding, checkout, or wizard flow advancing through numbered steps.

components.name: UI Switch
components.description: A switch whose checked/unchecked state is a pure function of the timeline; the track fill and sliding thumb are keyframed presets.
components.useFor: Showing a toggle being flipped in a settings panel walkthrough.

components.name: UI Tabs
components.description: A tabs widget whose active-tab state is a pure function of the timeline; the sliding indicator, label colors, and panel crossfade are keyframed/derived presets.
components.useFor: Showing a tabbed UI switching between content panels in a product demo.

components.name: UI Toast
components.description: A toast notification whose hidden/visible state is a pure function of the timeline. The Toast renderer is a pure function of a ToastStyle (opacity, translateY, scale); useToastTransition eases both the slide-in enter and the auto-dismiss exit. Variants default/success/error change the leading icon and its color.
components.useFor: Showing a success/error notification appear after an action (form submit, save, API call).

components.name: UI Toggle Group
components.description: A segmented control whose active value is a pure function of the timeline; a raised thumb SLIDES between segments (position + width derived from a float indicator offset, no jumps) and the labels crossfade color via mixOklch. The tabs precedent without content panels.
components.useFor: Showing a segmented control switching between view modes, time ranges, or mutually exclusive options.

components.name: UI Tooltip
components.description: A tooltip whose hidden/visible state is a pure function of the timeline. The Tooltip renderer is a pure function of a TooltipStyle (opacity, scale, translate); useTooltipTransition eases both the show and the hide. The static `side` prop sets the enter translate axis and the arrow placement.
components.useFor: Showing a hover tooltip appearing next to a UI element in a product walkthrough.

components.name: UI Typing Indicator
components.description: A continuous typing animation: N dots bounce with a staggered sine wave. A motion atom — it reads the frame and takes color, size, gap, and speed props, defaulting to currentColor so it inherits the bubble it sits in.
components.useFor: Signalling that a reply or an answer is being composed — drop it inside a `message-bubble` or any container.
